_README: B1 SPEAKING — teacher examiner card, scored /20 on its own rubric.
Separate from tools/exam_b1_final.json so it can be printed for the examiner only.
Rendered by the same tool; a config with no written questions produces just the
cover and the card — no answer sheets, no answer key.
title: Speaking Examination
subtitle: Interview · Picture · Topic Talk
warning: EXAMINER COPY — DO NOT SHOW THIS PAPER TO THE CANDIDATE
instructions: Enter the candidate's name, class and number in the boxes above before you begin.
Run the three parts in order: A Interview, B Describe the picture, C Topic talk.
Keep to the timings shown on the examiner card. Do not exceed 10 minutes per candidate.
Score each of the four rubric rows from 1 to 5 as the candidate speaks, not afterwards.
Enter the total out of 20 in the box on the examiner card.
information: Part A carries 5 marks, Part B 5 marks and Part C 10 marks.
For Part B, use one picture card from Part III of the written paper (harbor, harvest or alley).
Allow the candidate ONE minute of preparation before the Part C talk.
This result is reported separately from the /100 written paper.

parts.label: Speaking — examiner card
parts.hint: TEACHER ONLY — do not give this page to students.  Total time: 8-10 minutes per student.

blocks.title: A · Interview
prompts: Tell me about your family and where you live.
What did you use to do in your free time when you were younger?
How long have you been studying English?
What are you going to do after this exam?

blocks.title: B · Describe the picture
prompts: Show the student one picture card from Part III (harbor, harvest or alley).
Describe what you can see in this picture.
What do you think the people are doing, and why?
Would you like to work in a place like this? Why / why not?

blocks.title: C · Topic talk
prompts: Give the student ONE minute to prepare, then TWO minutes to talk.
Topic 1: A person who has changed my life.
Topic 2: Something I used to believe when I was a child.
Follow-up: If you could change one thing about your city, what would you change?
